key_insight: Human hearing is better described as a continuous five-dimensional atlas of states and trajectories than as a set of discrete hearing “types.”
clinical_relevance: This framework could improve precision otology by capturing within-ear changes and individual patterns that conventional audiogram severity averages miss.
method: Integrated 33 datasets from 8 countries across 62 years
Built a model that reconstructs unseen audiograms to near-decibel accuracy
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation across 4.29 million audiograms, with the atlas reconstructing unseen audiograms to near-decibel accuracy and preserving clinical detail.
watch_item: Because the atlas is derived from pooled historical audiograms and calibration standards, real-world implementation may require careful harmonization and prospective validation.
paper_title: The Human Hearing Atlas: a canonical map of human hearing
